## What language runs the pipeline?

The title-classification pipeline is primarily **R**. R owns the database
schema, prompt publication, pending-title selection, response validation,
result application, status view, and CSV export.

Python is used only at the OpenAI Batch API boundary:

- upload and submit a reviewed JSONL batch;
- check the remote batch and retrieve its output; and
- build a retry batch for failed requests.

The shell scripts under `bin/linux/classification/` connect those R and Python
steps into one operating workflow.

This notebook is deliberately read-only. It checks the pipeline's work but
does not publish a version, build or submit a batch, apply results, update
scheduled state, or write an export.

## Pipeline map

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  A[Maintained prompt source<br/>prompts/title_classification] -->|R: publish_title_version.R| B[classification.title_versions]
  C[Reusable talent profile source] -->|R: build_talent_profile.R| D[catalog.talent_profiles]
  E[catalog.videos<br/>current titles and hashes] --> F[R: 08_build_batch_classification.R]
  B --> F
  D --> F
  F --> G[Reviewable Batch JSONL and manifest]
  G -->|Python: submit| H[OpenAI Batch API]
  H -->|Python: check and retrieve| I[Response JSONL]
  I -->|R: 09_apply_batch_classification.R| J[classification.title_classification_results]
  J --> K[classification.title_classification_status]
  E --> K
  K --> L[R: 05_export_results_csv.R]
  L --> M[Current and archived CSV exports]
  I --> N[ops.pipeline_runs]
```

## Parameters

Render the complete audit:

```bash
quarto render r_scripts/notebooks/tests/title_classification_pipeline.qmd
```

If Quarto stalls before it begins processing chunks, bypass the project renv
autoloader for this read-only audit while keeping the installed R library:

```bash
RENV_CONFIG_AUTOLOADER_ENABLED=FALSE \
  quarto render r_scripts/notebooks/tests/title_classification_pipeline.qmd
```

Limit status and row previews to one exact talent code:

```bash
quarto render r_scripts/notebooks/tests/title_classification_pipeline.qmd \
  -P talent_code:TER4
```

The optional parameters are:

- `talent_code`: exact `catalog.talents.talent_code`; null checks all talents.
- `recent_limit`: maximum recent result and pipeline-run rows to display.
- `pending_preview_limit`: maximum pending-title rows to display.

## Connect to the canonical database

```{r}
required_packages <- c("DBI", "duckdb", "here", "knitr")
missing_packages <- required_packages[
  !vapply(required_packages, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)
]
if (length(missing_packages) > 0L) {
  stop(
    "Install the required R packages before rendering: ",
    paste(missing_packages, collapse = ", "),
    call. = FALSE
  )
}

repo_root <- here::here()
source(here::here("r_scripts", "lib", "utils", "repo_env.R"))
source(here::here("r_scripts", "lib", "utils", "datalake_root.r"))
source(here::here("r_scripts", "lib", "duckdb", "db_connect.R"))

load_repo_env(repo_root = repo_root)
db_path <- talent_lakehouse_db_path()
if (!file.exists(db_path)) {
  stop("Unified talent lakehouse not found: ", db_path, call. = FALSE)
}

con <- duckdb_connect(db_path = db_path, read_only = TRUE)

talent_code <- params$talent_code
if (is.null(talent_code) || is.na(talent_code) || !nzchar(trimws(talent_code))) {
  talent_code <- NULL
} else {
  talent_code <- trimws(talent_code)
}

recent_limit <- as.integer(params$recent_limit)
pending_preview_limit <- as.integer(params$pending_preview_limit)
if (is.na(recent_limit) || recent_limit < 1L) recent_limit <- 20L
if (is.na(pending_preview_limit) || pending_preview_limit < 1L) {
  pending_preview_limit <- 50L
}

relation_exists <- function(schema_name, relation_name) {
  count <- DBI::dbGetQuery(
    con,
    paste(
      "SELECT COUNT(*) AS relation_count",
      "FROM information_schema.tables",
      "WHERE table_schema = ? AND table_name = ?"
    ),
    params = list(schema_name, relation_name)
  )$relation_count[[1]]
  count == 1L
}

query_with_talent <- function(select_sql, order_sql = "", limit = NULL) {
  where_sql <- ""
  query_params <- list()
  if (!is.null(talent_code)) {
    where_sql <- " WHERE talent_code = ?"
    query_params <- list(talent_code)
  }
  limit_sql <- if (is.null(limit)) "" else sprintf(" LIMIT %d", as.integer(limit))
  DBI::dbGetQuery(
    con,
    paste0(select_sql, where_sql, order_sql, limit_sql),
    params = query_params
  )
}

display_table <- function(rows, digits = 2L) {
  if (nrow(rows) == 0L) {
    return(knitr::kable(data.frame(message = "No rows matched.")))
  }
  knitr::kable(rows, digits = digits)
}

database_info <- data.frame(
  item = c("Database", "Scope", "Rendered at"),
  value = c(
    db_path,
    if (is.null(talent_code)) "All talent codes" else talent_code,
    format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", tz = "UTC")
  )
)
display_table(database_info)
```

## Schema preflight

Every relation below is required for the maintained title-classification
workflow. A missing relation means the lakehouse migration or schema setup is
incomplete.

```{r}
required_relations <- data.frame(
  schema_name = c(
    "catalog", "catalog", "catalog", "classification", "classification",
    "classification", "classification", "ops"
  ),
  relation_name = c(
    "videos", "talents", "talent_profiles", "title_versions",
    "title_classification_results", "title_classification_status",
    "title_classification_scheduled_state", "pipeline_runs"
  )
)
required_relations$available <- mapply(
  relation_exists,
  required_relations$schema_name,
  required_relations$relation_name
)
required_relations$status <- ifelse(required_relations$available, "PASS", "FAIL")
display_table(required_relations[, c("status", "schema_name", "relation_name")])

classification_ready <- all(required_relations$available)
if (!classification_ready) {
  stop(
    "Required classification relations are missing. Run the maintained schema migration before continuing.",
    call. = FALSE
  )
}
```

## Published title versions

There should be exactly one active version. A complete version contains the
prompt, instructions, definitions, and output schema needed to reproduce its
requests. Historical metadata-only versions remain useful for lineage but
cannot be used to build new requests.

```{r}
title_versions <- DBI::dbGetQuery(
  con,
  paste(
    "SELECT title_version_id, taxonomy_version, prompt_version, active,",
    "version_status, LEFT(checksum_sha256, 16) AS checksum_prefix,",
    "LENGTH(system_prompt) AS system_prompt_chars,",
    "LENGTH(instructions) AS instruction_chars,",
    "LENGTH(definitions_json) AS definitions_chars,",
    "LENGTH(output_schema_json) AS schema_chars,",
    "source_revision, created_at, updated_at",
    "FROM classification.title_versions",
    "ORDER BY active DESC, updated_at DESC"
  )
)
display_table(title_versions)
```

## Automated health checks

These checks test the structural invariants needed by incremental
classification. `Observed` provides the count behind each result so a failure
can be investigated directly.

```{r}
active_version_count <- DBI::dbGetQuery(
  con,
  "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM classification.title_versions WHERE active"
)$n[[1]]
active_complete_count <- DBI::dbGetQuery(
  con,
  paste(
    "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM classification.title_versions",
    "WHERE active AND version_status = 'complete'",
    "AND LENGTH(system_prompt) > 0 AND LENGTH(instructions) > 0",
    "AND LENGTH(definitions_json) > 2 AND LENGTH(output_schema_json) > 2",
    "AND LENGTH(checksum_sha256) > 0"
  )
)$n[[1]]
available_video_count <- DBI::dbGetQuery(
  con,
  "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM catalog.videos WHERE is_available"
)$n[[1]]
status_video_count <- DBI::dbGetQuery(
  con,
  "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM classification.title_classification_status"
)$n[[1]]
duplicate_status_count <- DBI::dbGetQuery(
  con,
  paste(
    "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM (",
    "SELECT video_id, COUNT(*) AS copies",
    "FROM classification.title_classification_status",
    "GROUP BY video_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1",
    ")"
  )
)$n[[1]]
invalid_status_count <- DBI::dbGetQuery(
  con,
  paste(
    "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n",
    "FROM classification.title_classification_status",
    "WHERE classification_status NOT IN",
    "('classified', 'changed_title', 'new_or_unclassified')",
    "OR (is_classified AND classification_status <> 'classified')",
    "OR (NOT is_classified AND classification_status = 'classified')"
  )
)$n[[1]]
missing_version_lineage <- DBI::dbGetQuery(
  con,
  paste(
    "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n",
    "FROM classification.title_classification_results",
    "WHERE title_version_id IS NULL"
  )
)$n[[1]]
active_missing_profile <- DBI::dbGetQuery(
  con,
  paste(
    "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n",
    "FROM classification.title_classification_results AS result",
    "JOIN classification.title_versions AS version",
    "ON version.title_version_id = result.title_version_id",
    "WHERE version.active AND result.profile_id IS NULL"
  )
)$n[[1]]
orphaned_active_profiles <- DBI::dbGetQuery(
  con,
  paste(
    "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n",
    "FROM classification.title_classification_results AS result",
    "JOIN classification.title_versions AS version",
    "ON version.title_version_id = result.title_version_id",
    "LEFT JOIN catalog.talent_profiles AS profile",
    "ON profile.profile_id = result.profile_id",
    "WHERE version.active AND result.profile_id IS NOT NULL",
    "AND profile.profile_id IS NULL"
  )
)$n[[1]]

health_checks <- data.frame(
  check = c(
    "Exactly one active title version",
    "Active version has a complete prompt bundle",
    "Status view covers every available video",
    "Status view has one row per video",
    "Status labels agree with is_classified",
    "Every result has title-version lineage",
    "Active-version results have profile lineage",
    "Active-version profile IDs resolve"
  ),
  observed = c(
    active_version_count,
    active_complete_count,
    paste(status_video_count, "of", available_video_count),
    duplicate_status_count,
    invalid_status_count,
    missing_version_lineage,
    active_missing_profile,
    orphaned_active_profiles
  ),
  pass = c(
    active_version_count == 1L,
    active_complete_count == 1L,
    status_video_count == available_video_count,
    duplicate_status_count == 0L,
    invalid_status_count == 0L,
    missing_version_lineage == 0L,
    active_missing_profile == 0L,
    orphaned_active_profiles == 0L
  )
)
health_checks$status <- ifelse(health_checks$pass, "PASS", "FAIL")
display_table(health_checks[, c("status", "check", "observed")])
```

## Current classification status

The next normal batch selects `changed_title` and `new_or_unclassified` rows.
It skips `classified` rows because an exact result already exists for the
current `(video_id, title_hash, title_version_id)`.

```{r}
status_summary <- query_with_talent(
  paste(
    "SELECT talent_code, classification_status, COUNT(*) AS videos",
    "FROM classification.title_classification_status"
  ),
  order_sql = paste(
    " GROUP BY talent_code, classification_status",
    "ORDER BY talent_code, classification_status"
  )
)
display_table(status_summary)
```

```{r}
status_totals <- query_with_talent(
  paste(
    "SELECT classification_status, COUNT(*) AS videos",
    "FROM classification.title_classification_status"
  ),
  order_sql = paste(
    " GROUP BY classification_status",
    "ORDER BY CASE classification_status",
    "WHEN 'classified' THEN 1",
    "WHEN 'changed_title' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END"
  )
)
status_totals$selected_by_normal_batch <- status_totals$classification_status != "classified"
display_table(status_totals)
```

### Pending-title preview

This is a read-only preview of the rows that a normal build would select. It
does not use `--force-reclassify`.

```{r}
pending_where <- paste(
  "WHERE status.classification_status IN",
  "('changed_title', 'new_or_unclassified')"
)
pending_params <- list()
if (!is.null(talent_code)) {
  pending_where <- paste(pending_where, "AND status.talent_code = ?")
  pending_params <- list(talent_code)
}
pending_preview <- DBI::dbGetQuery(
  con,
  paste0(
    "SELECT status.video_id, status.talent_code, status.title,",
    "video.content_type, status.published_at, status.classification_status,",
    "LEFT(status.title_hash, 16) AS current_hash_prefix ",
    "FROM classification.title_classification_status AS status ",
    "JOIN catalog.videos AS video USING (video_id) ",
    pending_where,
    " ORDER BY published_at DESC, video_id LIMIT ",
    pending_preview_limit
  ),
  params = pending_params
)
display_table(pending_preview)
```

## Talent-profile coverage

Profiles are generic reusable records in `catalog.talent_profiles`. Title
classification uses the `contexts.title_classification` portion of the JSON
profile. Each current talent should resolve either to an exact active profile
or to an active default profile whose `talent_code` is null.

```{r}
profiles <- DBI::dbGetQuery(
  con,
  paste(
    "SELECT profile_id, talent_code, display_name, profile_version, active,",
    "LEFT(checksum_sha256, 16) AS checksum_prefix,",
    "source_pipeline_run_id, created_at, updated_at",
    "FROM catalog.talent_profiles",
    "ORDER BY active DESC, talent_code NULLS LAST, updated_at DESC"
  )
)
display_table(profiles)
```

```{r}
profile_coverage <- DBI::dbGetQuery(
  con,
  paste(
    "WITH current_talents AS (",
    "SELECT video.talent_code, talent.talent_name, COUNT(*) AS available_videos",
    "FROM catalog.videos AS video",
    "LEFT JOIN catalog.talents AS talent USING (talent_code)",
    "WHERE video.is_available",
    "GROUP BY video.talent_code, talent.talent_name",
    "), default_profile AS (",
    "SELECT COUNT(*) > 0 AS available",
    "FROM catalog.talent_profiles WHERE active AND talent_code IS NULL",
    ")",
    "SELECT current_talents.*,",
    "exact_profile.profile_id AS exact_active_profile_id,",
    "exact_profile.profile_version,",
    "CASE WHEN exact_profile.profile_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'exact'",
    "WHEN default_profile.available THEN 'default' ELSE 'missing' END",
    "AS resolution",
    "FROM current_talents",
    "LEFT JOIN catalog.talent_profiles AS exact_profile",
    "ON exact_profile.talent_code = current_talents.talent_code",
    "AND exact_profile.active",
    "CROSS JOIN default_profile",
    "ORDER BY current_talents.talent_code"
  )
)
if (!is.null(talent_code)) {
  profile_coverage <- profile_coverage[profile_coverage$talent_code == talent_code, , drop = FALSE]
}
display_table(profile_coverage)
```

## Recent applied results

Only results matching the video's current title hash are shown here. Changed
titles remain visible in the status and CSV audit fields, but their previous
classification is not represented as current work.

```{r}
recent_where <- "WHERE result_rank = 1"
recent_params <- list()
if (!is.null(talent_code)) {
  recent_where <- paste(recent_where, "AND talent_code = ?")
  recent_params <- list(talent_code)
}
recent_results <- DBI::dbGetQuery(
  con,
  paste0(
    "WITH ranked AS (",
    "SELECT result.created_at, result.video_id, result.talent_code,",
    "video.title, result.model, result.confidence, result.title_version_id,",
    "result.profile_id, result.pipeline_run_id,",
    "ROW_NUMBER() OVER (",
    "PARTITION BY result.video_id, result.title_version_id, result.title_hash ",
    "ORDER BY result.created_at DESC",
    ") AS result_rank ",
    "FROM classification.title_classification_results AS result ",
    "JOIN catalog.videos AS video ON video.video_id = result.video_id ",
    "JOIN classification.title_classification_status AS status ",
    "ON status.video_id = result.video_id ",
    "AND status.title_version_id = result.title_version_id ",
    "AND status.title_hash = result.title_hash ",
    "JOIN classification.title_versions AS version ",
    "ON version.title_version_id = result.title_version_id AND version.active",
    ") SELECT created_at, video_id, talent_code, title, model, confidence,",
    "title_version_id, profile_id, pipeline_run_id FROM ranked ",
    recent_where,
    " ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT ",
    recent_limit
  ),
  params = recent_params
)
display_table(recent_results)
```

## Recent pipeline runs

Applying a classification batch and publishing a talent profile register
executions in the shared `ops.pipeline_runs` relation.

```{r}
recent_runs <- DBI::dbGetQuery(
  con,
  paste0(
    "SELECT pipeline_run_id, pipeline_name, started_at, completed_at, status,",
    "error_summary FROM ops.pipeline_runs ",
    "WHERE pipeline_name IN ('title_classification', 'talent_profile_builder') ",
    "ORDER BY started_at DESC LIMIT ",
    recent_limit
  )
)
display_table(recent_runs)
```

## Scheduled batch state

The scheduled workflow stores its active state in DuckDB instead of a local
state JSON file or standalone classification database. No row means there is no
currently recorded pending scheduled batch.

```{r}
scheduled_state <- DBI::dbGetQuery(
  con,
  paste(
    "SELECT state_key, status, batch_id, request_count, pending_rows,",
    "created_at, submitted_at, last_checked_at, applied_at, updated_at, run_dir",
    "FROM classification.title_classification_scheduled_state",
    "ORDER BY updated_at DESC"
  )
)
display_table(scheduled_state)
```

## Current CSV export

The CSV is a delivery artifact generated from the unified DuckDB. It is not the
source used to determine pending work.

```{r}
export_path <- file.path(
  dirname(normalizePath(get_datalake_root(), winslash = "/", mustWork = FALSE)),
  "Processed",
  "Title_classification",
  "current",
  "classification_export_current.csv"
)
if (file.exists(export_path)) {
  export_info <- file.info(export_path)
  header <- names(utils::read.csv(
    export_path,
    nrows = 1L,
    check.names = FALSE,
    fileEncoding = "UTF-8"
  ))
  required_audit_columns <- c(
    "classification_status",
    "is_classified",
    "classified_title_hash",
    "current_title_hash"
  )
  export_check <- data.frame(
    item = c(
      "Path",
      "Exists",
      "Modified UTC",
      "Size bytes",
      "Has status/hash audit columns"
    ),
    value = c(
      export_path,
      "yes",
      format(export_info$mtime[[1]], "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", tz = "UTC"),
      as.character(export_info$size[[1]]),
      if (all(required_audit_columns %in% header)) "yes" else "no"
    )
  )
} else {
  export_check <- data.frame(
    item = c("Path", "Exists"),
    value = c(export_path, "no")
  )
}
display_table(export_check)
```

Refresh the current CSV manually when needed:

```bash
Rscript r_scripts/run/title_classification/05_export_results_csv.R
```

## Operating checklist

1. Render this notebook and investigate any failed health checks.
2. Review `changed_title` and `new_or_unclassified` counts.
3. Build a pending batch. Building is local and does not submit it.
4. Inspect the generated manifest and JSONL in the run directory.
5. Submit explicitly, then check and retrieve the completed response.
6. Run preview mode and review the flattened classifications.
7. Apply the response transactionally; the wrapper also refreshes CSV exports.
8. Render this notebook again and confirm the pending counts decreased as
   expected, the recent run completed, and the export modification time moved
   forward.

Build pending titles:

```bash
bin/linux/classification/run_title_classification_batch.sh \
  --run-id "title_$(date +%Y-%m-%d_%H-%M-%S)" \
  -- --batch-size 25
```

Submit only after review:

```bash
bin/linux/classification/run_title_classification_batch.sh \
  --mode submit \
  --run-dir PATH \
  --execute
```

Retrieve a completed batch:

```bash
bin/linux/classification/run_title_classification_batch.sh \
  --mode check \
  --run-dir PATH \
  --retrieve-output
```

Validate and preview the response without writing to DuckDB:

```bash
bin/linux/classification/run_title_classification_batch.sh \
  --mode preview \
  --run-dir PATH
```

Apply and refresh exports:

```bash
bin/linux/classification/run_title_classification_batch.sh \
  --mode apply \
  --run-dir PATH
```

Use `--force-reclassify` only when intentionally rebuilding every title in
scope. Under normal operation, unchanged current title/version pairs are
skipped automatically.

For a full incremental backfill, build review artifacts without submitting:

```bash
bin/linux/classification/run_title_classification_weekly.sh \
  --model gpt-5.6-terra \
  --batch-size 25
```

Add `--execute` to start or advance the durable batch lifecycle. The weekly
user-systemd timer starts this command Monday at 03:00 UTC; the hourly checker
uses `run_title_classification_scheduled.sh --check-only` to retrieve, validate,
apply, export, and retry active work without starting an extra batch.

```{r}
#| include: false
DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)
```
